item.title: Silicon Valley Bank: The $2.25bn Share Sale That Started a Run
item.description: Silicon Valley Bank looked fine on paper. About 42 hours after it announced a $2.25 billion share sale, regulators shut it down. How announcing a fix can start a bank run, and who came out ahead.

item.title: What Does an Investment Bank Actually Do?
item.description: What does an investment bank do? Sunny sells $1 million of new shares: the advisers, the bookrunner's book, the trading floor, and Morgan Stanley's two jobs.

item.title: What Is a Bond? Loans vs Bonds With a Lemonade Stand
item.description: What is a bond? A loan's three parts, why Sunny splits $100,000 into 100 bonds, bond vs share, and why $6 billion of Twitter bonds never sold.

item.title: Figma IPO: $3.5 Billion Left on the Table, by Bloomberg's Count
item.description: The banks priced Figma's IPO at $33 a share on 30 July 2025, and the next day it closed at $115.50, up 250%. Who left more than $3.5 billion on the table, by Bloomberg's count, why the bookrunners priced it there, and what happened next.

item.title: What Is a Share? Stocks Explained With a Lemonade Stand
item.description: What is a share? Sunny cuts her lemonade business into 100 pieces: what a share gives you, who sets its price, and why Figma's founder kept most of the votes.

item.title: Debt vs Equity, Explained With a Lemonade Stand
item.description: Debt vs equity from zero: Sunny needs $10,000 for a food truck. Borrow from a bank or give a partner 40%? What each costs, and how Musk used both to buy Twitter.

item.title: Credit Suisse: How $17 Billion of AT1 Bonds Were Wiped Out in One Weekend
item.description: On Sunday 19 March 2023, Credit Suisse's AT1 bonds, about 16 billion Swiss francs, were written down to zero while shareholders still got 3 billion francs. How AT1s work, what happened that weekend and what the courts said.

item.title: How Elon Musk's $44 Billion Twitter Deal Was Actually Financed
item.description: Seven banks committed $13 billion so Elon Musk could buy Twitter. The four debt tranches, who committed what, why the banks were stuck with the loans for 30 months, and what it really cost them.
